front.title: The Vacation Rental Protocol (VRP): Host-Domain Discovery and Verification of Signed Stay Offers

abstract.t:
The Vacation Rental Protocol (VRP) lets an AI agent or other client verify, directly from a vacation-rental host's own domain and with no intermediary, that a stay offer was signed by a key that domain publishes, has not been altered, and is within its stated lifetime. The signed offer carries the host domain's own statements of availability and exact price for the stay asked for. A valid signature proves the provenance and integrity of those statements; it does not guarantee that the stay is in fact available. A host domain publishes a discovery document at a well-known URI, an Ed25519 key set, and signed stay offers (compact JSON Web Signatures). Verification requires no central registry, issuer, accreditation program, or gatekeeper: control of the host domain is the root of trust.
This document specifies the discovery document, key publication and rotation, the signed verified stay offer, and the verification procedure, including fail-closed behavior and a three-state verification model. It also describes the existing provisional registration of the "vacation-rental.json" well-known URI suffix.
